creator: codex
subtasks: S1 execution-lease data plane: owner identity (instance id + started_at) + lease record (thread_id -> owner / acquired_at / heartbeat_at / expires_at / state) + acquire / renew / release / expire_scan. WRITE-ONLY: _background_tasks still decides everything, zero outward behaviour change. New module backend/db/execution_leases.py following the workflow_events in-module fallback precedent.

S2 status derivation reads the lease: has_active_task is answered by the lease instead of the in-process registry; /status and /list orphan semantics change from 'no task in this process' to 'lease expired'. Existing tripwires reshaped by design (not deleted): test_orphan_detection, test_workflow_stale, test_runner_phase_sync, plus the integration files that poke _background_tasks.

S3 automatic takeover of expired leases: startup + periodic scan resuming from the checkpoint. Takeover may resume the execution loop but may NOT make a decision for a human -- side-effecting nodes (publish/login/upload) are never re-run automatically; those park in a human-decision state and emit an event. Same rule as P2a-S4b's default-refuse and P0-W4's unknown reconciliation.

S4 move long tasks out of the orchestration process -- EVIDENCE-GATED (ruling 1): if S1-S3 yield no observable evidence of a long task occupying the API process, this degrades to a document + per-call-site classification (facts 9 and 13). Note fact 9: Chrome already runs on the host, so this is about the CDP client session, not about moving Chrome.

S5 docs/execution-plane.md: what the lease guarantees and does not guarantee, the single-process reality vs the topology docs/deployment.md describes, the no-DB semantics (durability: none), the automatic-takeover safety boundary, and the per-call-site classification.
notes: PLANNING ROUND (feat/p2b-s1-execution-lease, commit b69883e1) -- reconnaissance and slice plan, no code yet. The ticket was blank (status planning, subtasks [], placeholder jsonl), so this round produced prd.md: fifteen findings each with file:line, a five-slice plan, red lines, acceptance, and the rulings. THE TICKET'S PREMISE WAS REWRITTEN: Dockerfile:81 runs `uvicorn backend.api.app:app --port 8889` with NO --workers, so production is SINGLE-PROCESS (P0's own verification says so at research/p0-claims-verification.md:24) while docs/deployment.md documents a load-balanced three-replica, four-worker topology -- documented end state, not fact. So 'the API process does not hold the real execution lifecycle' is not a defect happening today; what IS happening is that a deploy kills in-flight work and the orphan is only detected, never taken over. Findings that carry the plan: (1) _background_tasks (api/routes/_runner.py:42) documents its own boundary -- cleared on restart, DB rows left at 'running' are 'restart orphans, detected lazily in /list and /status (no startup scan)'; (2) FOUR pieces of process-local state decide what callers observe (_LAST_HISTORY_WRITE, _active_sync_executions, _background_tasks, _last_status at _runner.py:33-45); (3) derive_status(..., has_active_task=True) (state/machine.py:34, priority 9/10 at :129-135) makes RUNNING vs STALE a question about THIS process -- the same checkpoint read elsewhere is a different status; (4) _is_orphan_running (api/routes/workflow.py:389-399) is 'task is None or task.done()', so 'orphan' means 'this process does not have it'; (5) recovery already exists and is human-triggered (POST /recover/{thread_id} at workflow.py:1623, retry_from_last_success via Command(goto=) at :475-491) -- detection exists, automatic takeover does not; (6) there is NO lease/heartbeat/worker/job-queue anywhere in backend/, so the durable scheduler is built from zero; (7) Chrome ALREADY runs out of process on the HOST (docs/deployment.md:284-407), so moving 'XHS Browser' means the CDP client session, not Chrome; (8) db/pool.py is Postgres-only (SQLite is only the dev checkpointer fallback, graph/builder.py:432,612) and the db/ fallback pattern is inconsistent -- workflow_events.py:62-71 has an in-module _mem_events fallback while db/workflows.py has ZERO is_pool_ready checks (the guard is pushed to callers at _runner._db_upsert:71-74). Dependency check: P0's retry consolidation IS delivered (graph/error_handling.py exhaustive RETRY_POLICIES + get_retry_policy raising KeyError), and its comment assigns the 'unified retry engine' to P1/P2 -- recorded as an explicit non-goal. RULINGS (user, 2026-09-16): (1) S4 is evidence-gated -- S1-S3 first, independent worker only if the evidence demands it, else S4 degrades to doc + call-site classification; (2) when is_pool_ready() is false the lease degrades EXPLICITLY with a single reader answering 'durability: none' -- never a silent downgrade, and never fail-closed (that would kill local dev and the whole test suite). Ruling 3 (adopted by discipline, not escalated): automatic takeover may resume the loop but may never re-run a side-effecting node. Tripwires to reshape by design: test_orphan_detection(4), test_workflow_stale(7), test_recover(11), test_publish_retry(8), test_runner_phase_sync(4) plus test_api_routes / test_sse_eventbus / test_workflow_bug_fixes.
